question:
For natural k define the canonical real source coefficient polynomial by a_{k,r}=sum_{m=0}^r C(k+r-m,k)/m! for0<=r<=k and A_k(t)=sum_{r=0}^k a_{k,r}t^r. Equivalently it is the degree-k truncation of the formal series exp(t)/(1-t)^(k+1). Let F_k(t)=(1-t)^(k+1)A_k(t), H_k(t)=exp(-1)F_k(t)+F_k(1-t), and S_k(p)=H_k(p+1).

The predecessor specified only that A_k had degree<=k and asked why the endpoint values were exp(-1) and1. Explain why that degree condition alone cannot determine those values, using k=0 and a suitable constant-polynomial example. For the actual coefficient definition above, derive A_k(0)=1 rather than assuming it.

Explain why t=p+1 sends p=-1,0 to t=0,1 with no derivative scaling. Show how the two endpoint factors make each contribution and its derivatives of orders0,...,k vanish at the OPPOSITE endpoint, and then compute S_k(-1) and S_k(0). Distinguish this opposite-endpoint decoupling from specifying every derivative at the contribution's own endpoint; a full higher-jet derivation is not requested here.

Finally write the exact reflected expression H_k(1-t). State precisely what it means for reflection to exchange the two endpoint SHAPES and their assigned weights. Is H_k literally reflection invariant, or does H_k(1-t)=c H_k(t) hold for some fixed scalar c for all t? Decide this by its endpoint values. Include k=0 and preserve which shape carries exp(-1); do not move that weight to the other endpoint in the definition of the unreflected source.
reference_answer:
A degree bound alone says nothing about the constant coefficient. If k=0 and A_0=2, then the displayed generic weighted endpoint form is2exp(-1)(1-t)+2t; its endpoint values are2exp(-1) and2, not the requested values. This does not refute the actual canonical source polynomial; it shows why the predecessor's standalone description omitted load-bearing normalization. In the canonical definition, a_{k,0}=C(k,k)/0!=1, and evaluating A_k at0 retains exactly that constant coefficient. Thus A_k(0)=1 for every k. This follows from the supplied finite source coefficients, not from degree<=k or a new normalization hypothesis.

Set t=p+1. Then p=-1 gives t=0, p=0 gives t=1 and dt/dp=1, so ordinary differentiation in p adds no scale factor. F_k(t) has the factor(1-t)^(k+1); by repeated product differentiation, every derivative of order j<=k still vanishes at t=1. Its reflection F_k(1-t)=t^(k+1)A_k(1-t) and its derivatives through order k vanish at t=0. Therefore the unreflected exp(-1)F_k term contributes no k-jet at the right node, while the reflected F_k(1-t) term contributes no k-jet at the left node. Those opposite-node zeros decouple the two contributions. They alone would not determine all derivatives at the responsible node; the actual coefficient identities supply further own-node information, outside this question's requested proof.

For the endpoint values, F_k(0)=A_k(0)=1 and F_k(1)=0 because k+1>=1. Thus H_k(0)=exp(-1),H_k(1)=1 and S_k(-1)=exp(-1),S_k(0)=1, with the exponential weight on the UNREFLECTED F_k term. No interior or nonzero-k assumption is needed. At k=0,A_0=1,F_0(t)=1-t and H_0(t)=exp(-1)(1-t)+t.

The exact reflected expression is H_k(1-t)=exp(-1)F_k(1-t)+F_k(t). Reflection exchanges the ordered shape pair(F_k(t),F_k(1-t)). Expressed again against the unreflected ordered pair, the weights change from(exp(-1),1) to(1,exp(-1)). More generally H_{a,b}(t)=aF_k(t)+bF_k(1-t) obeys H_{a,b}(1-t)=H_{b,a}(t). This is weighted SHAPE exchange, not invariance of the fixed-weight polynomial. Literal invariance already fails because H_k(0)!=H_k(1). If H_k(1-t)=c H_k(t) held for all t, t=0 would give c=exp(1), while t=1 would give c=exp(-1); these are unequal. Thus no such fixed scalar exists. The k=0 linear example shows the same failure directly.

This is the same canonical endpoint decomposition in the production definitions. The corrected question makes its coefficient normalization explicit and replaces ambiguous 'symmetry up to a constant' by an exact weighted-reflection identity. Static inspection of the local source/theorem proofs is not new Lean execution, a new circuit/resource theorem or an external-paper fidelity seal.
